member.name: T:StreamHash.Core.IStreamingHash`1
member.summary: Interface for streaming hash algorithms that can process data incrementally.
member.typeparam: The type of the hash result (uint, ulong, byte[], UInt128, etc.)

remarks.para: Streaming hash algorithms allow data to be processed in chunks rather than all at once, enabling constant memory usage regardless of input size.
Thread Safety: Implementations are NOT thread-safe. Each thread should use its own instance.

member.name: P:StreamHash.Core.IStreamingHash`1.BlockSize
member.summary: Gets the block size in bytes that the algorithm processes internally.

remarks.para: Data is buffered until a complete block is available for processing. For optimal performance, provide data in multiples of this block size.

Common block sizes:
MurmurHash3-32: 4 bytes
MurmurHash3-128: 16 bytes
CityHash64: 32 bytes
CityHash128: 16 bytes
SpookyHash: 96 bytes
SipHash: 8 bytes
FarmHash: 64 bytes
HighwayHash: 32 bytes

member.name: P:StreamHash.Core.IStreamingHash`1.DigestSize
member.summary: Gets the size of the hash output in bytes.

remarks.para:
Common digest sizes:
32-bit hashes: 4 bytes
64-bit hashes: 8 bytes
128-bit hashes: 16 bytes

member.name: P:StreamHash.Core.IStreamingHash`1.TotalBytesProcessed
member.summary: Gets the total number of bytes that have been processed so far.
member.remarks: This includes both fully processed blocks and any pending data in the internal buffer.

member.name: M:StreamHash.Core.IStreamingHash`1.Update(System.ReadOnlySpan{System.Byte})
member.summary: Appends data to the hash computation.
member.param: The data to add to the hash computation.

remarks.para: Data is accumulated in an internal buffer until a complete block is available. When enough data is accumulated, full blocks are processed immediately.

list.item: Provide data in multiples of for best performance
For file hashing, use a buffer size that is a multiple of the block size

member.name: M:StreamHash.Core.IStreamingHash`1.Finalize
member.summary: Completes the hash computation and returns the result.

remarks.para: After calling , the hasher is in an invalid state. Call before processing more data, or dispose and create a new instance.
This method processes any remaining buffered data with appropriate padding.

member.exception: Finalize has already been called without a subsequent Reset.

member.name: M:StreamHash.Core.IStreamingHash`1.Reset
member.summary: Resets the hasher to its initial state, ready to compute a new hash.

remarks.para: After calling , the hasher is in the same state as a newly created instance with the same seed/key parameters.

This method clears all internal state including:
Accumulated hash state
Internal buffer contents
Total bytes processed counter

member.name: T:StreamHash.Core.MurmurHash3_128
member.summary: Streaming implementation of MurmurHash3 128-bit x64 hash algorithm.

remarks.para: MurmurHash3 128-bit x64 is optimized for 64-bit processors and produces a 128-bit hash value, providing better collision resistance than the 32-bit variant.

list.item: Collision Resistance: Excellent for hash tables, NOT cryptographically secure
Optimized for 64-bit processors; use 32-bit variant on 32-bit systems
Processes 16 bytes per iteration for maximum throughput
Uses rotation and multiplication for mixing

member.name: T:StreamHash.Core.SipHash24
member.summary: Streaming implementation of SipHash-2-4, a cryptographically secure PRF.

remarks.para: SipHash is a family of pseudorandom functions (PRFs) optimized for short inputs. SipHash-2-4 uses 2 compression rounds and 4 finalization rounds.

list.item: PRF security: Output is indistinguishable from random given unknown key
Resistant to hash-flooding attacks on hash tables
NOT suitable for password hashing (use Argon2, bcrypt, etc.)
NOT collision-resistant without knowing the key
Hash table protection against algorithmic complexity attacks

member.name: T:StreamHash.Core.SpookyHash128
member.summary: Streaming implementation of SpookyHash V2 128-bit hash algorithm.

remarks.para: SpookyHash is a non-cryptographic hash function created by Bob Jenkins. Version 2 fixes a weakness in Version 1 and is the recommended version.

list.item: Block Size: 96 bytes (optimal), processes 8 bytes at a time
Collision Resistance: Excellent for hash tables, NOT cryptographically secure
Every bit of the input affects every bit of the output

remarks.para: Short vs Long Input: SpookyHash uses different code paths for short (<192 bytes) and long inputs to optimize performance. This streaming implementation handles both cases.
